source: USFS / NPS Backcountry Safety & Leave No Trace Seven Principles
safety_rules: Always leave a trip plan (Leave-Behind Safety Card) with a trusted contact before entering the backcountry.
Set a hard turnaround time before starting: reaching the summit is optional; returning to the trailhead safely is mandatory.
Phone GPS works in Airplane Mode without cell service, but cold temperatures drain lithium batteries rapidly—keep your phone in an inside pocket.
Never rely solely on a battery-powered device; carry a paper Trailhead Sheet and compass.
Treat all backcountry surface water (streams, lakes, springs) via filtration (0.1 micron) or chemical/boiling purification.
Above treeline (e.g., Franconia Ridge, Mt. Washington, Rocky Mountain alpine tundra), turn back immediately if thunder is heard or cumulus clouds build.
leave_no_trace: Travel and camp on durable surfaces.
Dispose of waste properly (pack it in, pack it out).
